1  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT
In this appeal, petitioner is seeking for enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 08.06.2013 at 11:00.p.m., there was an accident involving the Moped bearing No.KA-01-EK-0245 and lorry bearing No.KA-32-A-0838, wherein the petitioner sustained the injuries as a pillion rider of the moped.
He was treated at Manipal Hospital and Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital.
The claim of the petitioner before the Tribunal was opposed by respondent No.1-Insurance Company.
The Tribunal after taking evidence and hearing both the parties, allowed the claim petition awarding compensation of Rs.6,54,378/- with 6% interest per annum.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement the petitioner is before this Court.

Heard the arguments of Sri. K.Shanthraj., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.
Manjula.N.Tejaswi., learned counsel for respondent No.1-Insurance Company.
5.

It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was aged 22 years, he was earning a sum of Rs.12,000/-per month as a medical store sales and delivery boy in Mini International Distributors.
The Tribunal has taken his income at Rs.5,000/- and applied the multiplier '17'.

Through PW.3-Medical evidence is placed explaining 25% of whole body disability,
the Tribunal considered disability at 15%, future medical expenses, compensation towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities and discomfort are on the lower side and sought for enhancement of compensation.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1-Insurance Company contended that though the Insurance Company has satisfied the award of the Tribunal, the petitioner after treatment became normal and he is working.
There is no loss of future income.
Medical expenses was fully reimbursed and percentage of disability assessed by PW.3-Doctor to the lower limb
was at 50%, whereas whole body it was assessed at 25%.

The Tribunal has properly considered 1/3rd of the limb NC:
2024:KHC:32996 disability and assessed the loss of future earnings.
There is no ground for enhancement of compensation and supported the impugned judgment.

sentences.text: I have given my anxious consideration to arguments addressed on behalf of both the sides and perused the material on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident, injury sustained by the petitioner and being a victim of the accident entitled to claim compensation.
Ex.P.4-wound certificate point out the "deglowing injury of both the foot with exposed tendons".
He has also suffered dislocation of left elbow.
PW.3-Dr.S.A.Somashekar, the Orthopedic Surgeon of Bowring hospital though not a treated doctor in his evidence explains the limb disability of 50%.
Taking into consideration, the age of the petitioner, his avocation, the injuries certainly will affect the earning capacity of the petitioner.
The Tribunal has considered 1/3rd of the limb disability.
But circumstances forces to assess the limb disability at 20% instead of 15% taken by the Tribunal.
9. The petitioner requires a surgery and the insertion of an implant, which required minimum Rs.20,000/-.
Compared NC: 2024:KHC:32996 to the medical expenses, the future medical expenses assessed is Rs.20,000/- is reasonable.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.20,000/- towards pain and agony and loss of amenities, which are not comparable.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled towards pain and sufferings at Rs.60,000/-, Rs.60,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

Food,
nourishment and attendant charges Rs.20,000/- assessed by the Tribunal and conveyance of Rs.15,000/- is kept intact.

Medical expenses of Rs.4,07,378/- is reimbursed by the Tribunal .
10.
In so far as the loss of future income is concerned, in the year 2013, the person with no proof of income, will earn not less than Rs.8,000/-.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be taken as Rs.8,000/-.
Future loss of income comes to 8,000 X 12 X 18 X 20% = 3,45,000/- as against Rs.1,62,000/- assessed by the Tribunal.
The nature of injury certainly impact on the expectancy of the life of the petitioner.
Hence, Rs.25,000/- is assessed towards it.
Total compensation stands at Rs.9,52,978/- as against Rs.6,54,378/- as assessed by the Tribunal and thereby enhancement of Rs.2,98,600/-, which is rounded off to Rs.2,99,000/-.
It is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and NC: 2024:KHC:32996 circumstances of the case.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in result, the following:

ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part;
ii) The impugned judgment and award is modified;
iii) The petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,99,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization excluding interest on future medical expenses.
iv) Both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
v) Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation within 8 (eight) weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
